summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of ONGC's interim dividend announcement and the associated tax implications in India for FY27, with most factual claims verified by authoritative sources.

claims.claim: ONGC's board announced an interim dividend of 160% after its Q2 FY27 results on November 5, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm ONGC's board meeting on November 5, 2026, for Q2 FY27 results and the declaration of a 160% interim dividend.

claims.claim: This translates to a dividend payout of ₹8 per equity share, based on a face value of ₹5.
claims.note: Sources confirm the 160% dividend on a face value of ₹5 results in ₹8 per share.

claims.claim: The record date for determining eligible shareholders has been fixed as November 12, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple financial news outlets confirm November 12, 2026, as the record date for the interim dividend.

claims.claim: The company reported a significant rise in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) by 46.9% year-on-year to ₹18,534.82 crore for Q2 FY27.
claims.note: Several sources corroborate the consolidated PAT figure and the 46.9% year-on-year increase for Q2 FY27.

claims.claim: Consolidated Revenue from Operations: Rose by 25.6% year-on-year to ₹1,98,263.33 crore.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the consolidated revenue from operations and the 25.6% year-on-year increase.

claims.claim: Companies are required to deduct TDS on dividend payments if the aggregate dividend paid to a resident shareholder from a single company exceeds ₹10,000 in a financial year (effective from FY 2025-26 onwards, earlier it was ₹5,000). The TDS rate is typically 10% under Section 194 of the Income Tax Act.
claims.note: Multiple income tax sources confirm the TDS threshold for resident individuals increased to ₹10,000 from FY 2025-26 under Section 194, with a 10% TDS rate.

claims.claim: For NRIs, TDS on dividends is generally deducted at a rate of 20% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) as per Section 195 of the Income Tax Act.
claims.note: Sources confirm that TDS on dividends for NRIs is generally 20% (plus surcharge and cess) under Section 195, with DTAA potentially offering lower rates.

article_title: ONGC Interim Dividend 2026: What Investors Need to Know
